reason: The revision handles several difficult failures thoughtfully: application recovery compares changed fields and offers exact combined answers plus a private download; final submission validates receipts before clearing recovery; close-grading explicitly reconciles uncertain outcomes; batch release bounds waits and requires fresh review after uncertainty. The public mobile composition is coherent and restrained, states the no-fee semester proposition early, and distinguishes partnerships from approved work. However, the actual single-outcome release action still bypasses the safer acknowledgement model. That inconsistency at an irreversible operator action prevents world-class agreement. Local source and synthetic browser/SQL evidence support these strengths, but do not establish actual authenticated task completion or hosted reliability. Missing approved engagement evidence and workload facts also leave the broad purpose incompletely substantiated.

findings.evidence: ReleaseButton is rendered for locked decisions in admin/applications/[id]/page.tsx:552 and Hash (source references inspected). It calls useAction/runAction, which awaits authorizedFetch and response.json without a deadline, accepts every successful HTTP response including a null/malformed body, and maps transport loss to 'Could not release'. Only result.ok or released:true triggers refresh. The batch release tests in release-reliability.spec.ts exercise ReleaseAllButton, so their lost/stalled coverage does not cover this live alternative.
findings.userImpact: A stalled single release can remain at Releasing indefinitely. A committed release followed by response loss leaves a stale locked row and generic failure with retry available; a malformed successful response can announce release without a verified receipt. Operators receive different certainty for the same irreversible outcome depending on entry point.
findings.suggestedFix: Give single release the same bounded full-body wait, validated action-specific receipt, explicit unknown-outcome feedback and authoritative readback as batch release. Add focused single-release stalled-body, malformed-success and commit-then-lost-response checks.
